With DocGeo

DocGeo, the dynamic geometry software of DocTools, contains DocCells: a sheet next to a figure, each reading the other.

In DocGeo, File › View › New spreadsheet view adds a sheet next to the figure; File › Tab › New spreadsheet tab makes a tab of it.

The GEO function

In a cell, GEO reads the value of an object of the figure, given by its name in quotation marks.

=GEO("AB")
=2*GEO("r")+1
=GEO("'Figure 1'!c")
  • The cell follows the figure while it is being manipulated.
  • A point is read as the list of its coordinates: =GEO("A")*2 is a point too.
  • While typing a formula, a click on an object of the figure writes GEO and its name in it.
  • An unknown object gives #N/A. Outside DocGeo, GEO always gives #N/A.
  • GEO has the same name in all languages.

The figure reads the cells

In a DocGeo formula, !B3 is a cell, !B2:B21 a range.

Differences with DocCells alone

In DocGeo
Menus and buttonsin DocGeo's bars, when the sheet is active
FileDocGeo's: the sheet is saved in the .dgo, lists and links included
Sheetsone per view; several spreadsheet tabs read one another
UndoCtrl Z in the cells only undoes the cells

The spreadsheet page of the DocGeo manual gives the details.
